extracted.intended_audience: advanced TeX users, macro authors, and format/package implementers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and conventions used in plain.tex (the standard plain TeX format) for initializing TeX, allocating registers, defining private macros, choosing fonts, and providing formatting primitives so that independently developed macro packages can coexist and perform efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of private control sequence naming with @
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it easy for plain TeX to have private control sequences that cannot be redefined by ordinary users; all such control sequences will have at least one '@' in their names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During format initialization set \catcode'\@=11 so '@' behaves like a letter, define private macros containing '@', and later set \catcode'\@=12 so atsigns act like ordinary punctuation when TeX runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \dospecials for verbatim copying characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Define \dospecials to list all characters whose catcodes should probably be changed to 12 (other) when copying things verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plain format defines \dospecials as a list of \do\... entries; note that ASCII (null), (tab), (linefeed), (formfeed), (return) and (delete) are not included in the list. Appendix E shows how to use \dospecials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathcode initialization defaults and when to change
rubrics_metrics.description: INITEX initializes the \mathcode table: digits get \mathcode x = x + "7000, letters get x + "7100, and other characters get \mathcode x = x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is rarely need to change mathcodes; the plain format also sets mathcodes consistent with extended character sets and Computer Modern fonts. Exceptions exist for special delimiters or when intentionally overriding defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not change uccode/lccode except for extended alphabets
rubrics_metrics.description: INITEX makes \uccode'X='X, \uccode'x='X, \lccode'X='x, \lccode'x='x for letters and zero for nonletters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tables are used by \uppercase/\lowercase and hyphenation; changes should be made only in format packages that set TeX up for languages with more than 26 letters (see Chapter 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: sfcode defaults and French spacing support
rubrics_metrics.description: INITEX sets \sfcode table mostly to 1000, with \sfcode'X=999 for uppercase letters; some characters can be made transparent by setting their \sfcode to 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain.tex provides \frenchspacing and \nonfrenchspacing macros to change sfcodes of punctuation marks; see Chapter 12 for what an sfcode does.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delimiter codes and don't make braces delimiters
rubrics_metrics.description: INITEX sets all \delcode values to -1 (no characters recognized as delimiters), except \delcode'\. = 0 for a 'null delimiter'. Plain format sets nine delimiter values for Computer Modern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT set \delcode for '{' and '}' (leave equal to -1) because making braces delimiters is a big mistake: braces are used for grouping when supplying macro arguments and must not be used both as math delimiters and group delimiters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register-number allocation ground rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Macro writers should abide by ground rules for register usage so independent macro packages can coexist peacefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
1) Registers numbered 0–9 are always free for temporary 'scratch' use and are assumed clobbered. 2) Registers \count255, \dimen255, and \skip255 are freely available similarly. 3) All assignments to scratch registers numbered 1,3,5,7,9 should be \global; assignments to 0,2,4,6,8,255 should be non-\global (prevents 'save stack buildup'). 4) You may use any register within a group if grouping will restore it and other macros won't make global assignments. 5) When a register is used by several macros or over long spans use 
ewcount, 
ewdimen, 
ewbox, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name:
Use 
ewcount/
ewdimen/
ew... for long-term allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: For registers used across macros or for long-lived storage, allocate them with the provided \new... macros rather than assuming particular numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain.tex provides allocation macros that maintain counters (e.g. \count10..\count20) and an \allocationnumber that equals the most recently allocated number; macro packages should refer to \allocationnumber to find numbers that were allocated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation macros must check for room and log allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: The allocation macro \alloc@ does the allocation work and ensures there is still room; it writes messages into the log file about allocations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided \ch@ck (errmessage on no room) and \wlog to record "\maxdimen=\dimen10" style messages for debugging and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide small memory-efficient help texts via \newhelp
rubrics_metrics.description: \newhelp macro aids in creating home-made help texts by storing them in token registers rather than taking up token memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \newhelp\helpout{This is a help message.} and then \errhelp=\helpout before issuing an \errmessage; this makes efficient use of TeX's memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviate common constants to save memory and speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Define short control sequences for commonly used constants (e.g. \@ne = 1, \@M = 10000) to make TeX run a little faster and consume less memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The documentation may show long forms for readability, but plain.tex uses such abbreviations internally; keep private constants untouchable where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect a few fundamental constants (\maxdimen, \hideskip, \centering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain constants like \maxdimen, \hideskip, and \centering are essential and must not be changed under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either ignore these constants or use them as provided; the next four constants (\p@, \z@, \z@skip, \voidb@x) have private names so they are untouchable; \p@ is used as an abbreviation for '1pt' and \z@ for '0pt'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep preloaded fonts minimal but ensure core fonts present
rubrics_metrics.description: Most formats should keep the total number of preloaded fonts relatively small but ensure sixteen basic fonts (e.g., cmr10, cmr7, cmti10) are actually loaded for standardization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain.tex preloads a set of Computer Modern fonts and marks them with \preloaded, then \let\preloaded=\undefined to prevent direct use; local installations can change which extra fonts to preload depending on local conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \skewchar and math families appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Set \skewchar appropriately for math italic and math symbol fonts; group fonts into families for math and provide shorthand commands like \rm, \it, \cal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define \textfont, \scriptfont, \scriptscriptfont for families; create new families with \newfam for additional text-style commands (\it, \sl, \bf, \tt) and set the family font assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide pseudo-parameters in the format (e.g., \smallskipamount)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define pseudo-parameters in the format that behave like internal TeX parameters and that users are free to change, but which are part of the plain TeX format rather than primitives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Examples: \smallskipamount, \medskipamount,  igskipamount, 
ormalbaselineskip, 
ormallineskip, 
ormallineskiplimit, \jot. Use these to set consistent spacing defaults for the format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initialize many parameters to sensible defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain.tex assigns default values to a large number of parameters (e.g., \hbadness=1000, \tolerance=200, \hsize=6.5in, \parindent=20pt, \abovedisplayskip=12pt plus 3pt minus 9pt, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These defaults are part of the format and provide consistent behavior; some parameters are set by TeX at runtime and should not be initialized here (e.g., \time, \day, \month, \year, \outputpenalty, \predisplaysize, \displaywidth, \displayindent). See documentation for the full list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not initialize parameters that TeX sets at runtime
rubrics_metrics.description: Some parameters should not be initialized in the format because TeX assigns them dynamically during a run (e.g., \time, \day, \month, \year, \outputpenalty, \predisplaysize, \displaywidth, \displayindent, \looseness, \hangindent, \hangafter, \parshape).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize which quantities are computed by TeX just before or during processing and leave them alone in format initialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement \newif to create boolean trios
rubrics_metrics.description: \newif\iffoo creates three control sequences: \footrue, \foofalse, and \iffoo, with the condition initially false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The implementation uses temporary changes of \escapechar and \uppercase to automate generation of the pair; example usage: \newif\ifalpha creates \alphatrue, \alphafalse, and \ifalpha.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design \obeyspaces and \obeylines carefully with catcodes
rubrics_metrics.description: \obeyspaces sets the space character to active; \obeylines sets the end-of-line character active and lets it be \par.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \obeylines uses \let^^M=\par rather than \def so constructions like \let\par=\cr \obeylines \halign{...} work properly; be careful with catcode changes and trailing '%' in definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide loop/iteration macros using scratch control sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Define iteration constructs such as \loop...\repeat by storing the body in \body and using a scratch control sequence \next to iterate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The implementation sets \let\repeat=\fi so that \loop ... \if ... \repeat can be made skippable; use temporary \next values that don't persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate breakable vs non-breakable spaces and provide relative spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide spacing macros: \enskip, \quad, \qquad are breakable spaces (legitimate breakpoints); \enspace, \thinspace, \negthinspace produce non-breakable spaces (may disappear near certain breaks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All these spaces are relative to the current font; use \hglue( glue ) (\hglue) for horizontal space that never disappears and \vglue for vertical glue. Implementations should preserve \spacefactor across \hglue and \vglue operations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide penalty macros to control break desirability in appropriate modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Define \break, \nobreak, \allowbreak for general use; define \- and \slash for horizontal mode; define vertical-only penalties like \filbreak, \goodbreak, \eject, \supereject, and small/med/bigbreaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose penalty values appropriate to the intended effect (e.g., \penalty-10000 for forced break). Use \removelastskip helper to avoid redundant glue before inserting penalties and skips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement box and alignment utilities efficiently
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide \line, \leftline, \rightline, \centerline for full-line boxes; \llap and \rlap to make zero-width boxes; \underbar implemented via math mode; \strut implemented as a zero-width rule for minimal time/space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \m@th (set \mathsurround=0) where macros use math mode internally; implement \strut as a box created once (\strutbox) and copied/unhcopy to minimize cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabbing implementation keeps tab positions with boxes and uses \+ as outer
rubrics_metrics.description: Tabbing macros keep track of tab positions by maintaining boxes full of empty boxes having specified widths; \+ is defined as an outer macro (alias \tabalign) so TeX better detects runaway arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \settabs and \sett@b logic to build tab boxes; a non-outer \tabalign is provided for inner contexts. The best way to understand them is via simple examples and \tracingall.
